title: Unit 4 Solutions and Solubility Test
subject: chemistry
variation_policy: Preserve the exact 5-question written-response structure and mark balance while changing contexts, chemicals, and numerical values.

section_plans.title: Written Response
section_plans.instructions: Answer all questions. Show all work for calculations, include units, and use appropriate significant digits.

prebuilt_questions.stem: A window-cleaning solution is 18.5% (v/v) ammonia. If a bottle contains 750 mL of the solution, what volume of pure ammonia is present?
A solution is prepared by dissolving 0.180 mol of sodium carbonate, Na2CO3(s), to make 1.50 L of solution. What is the molar concentration of the solution?

A stock solution of 12.0 mol/L hydrochloric acid, HCl(aq), is available. What volume of stock solution is needed to prepare 500.0 mL of 1.50 mol/L HCl(aq)? Describe how you would prepare the solution.
prebuilt_questions.answer_hint: Use C1V1 = C2V2; V1 = (1.50 x 0.5000)/12.0 = 0.0625 L = 62.5 mL. Measure 62.5 mL of stock acid and dilute with water to a final volume of 500.0 mL.

prebuilt_questions.stem: If 18.0 mL of KOH(aq) is required to completely neutralize 25.0 mL of 0.150 mol/L H2SO4(aq), what is the concentration of the base? Write the balanced chemical equation, include states, then solve.
prebuilt_questions.answer_hint: H2SO4(aq) + 2KOH(aq) -> K2SO4(aq) + 2H2O(l); n(H2SO4) = 0.00375 mol, n(KOH) = 0.00750 mol, c(KOH) = 0.417 mol/L approximately

prebuilt_questions.stem: Describe one specific example of how water being a good solvent is an advantage and one specific example of how it can be a disadvantage. Explain each example using chemistry ideas.
prebuilt_questions.answer_hint: Strong responses connect water polarity to dissolving ionic or polar substances as a benefit and explain a drawback such as corrosion, contamination transport, or inability to dissolve non-polar materials well.

generation_constraints: Generate exactly 5 written-response questions worth 20 marks total.
Include one percent by volume question.
Include one molar concentration question from moles and solution volume.
Include one dilution question that also asks how to prepare the solution.
Include one neutralization question that requires a balanced equation with states before solving.
Include one conceptual explanation question about water as a solvent.
